news.title: Ireland's Women's Football Team To Face Poland In World Cup Bid
news.lede: The Republic of Ireland will face Poland for a place at next year's World Cup in Brazil. Carla Ward's side eased past Kazakhstan in their playoff semi-final last night, winning 12-nil on aggregate. The Girls in Green missed out on qualifying for the 2025 Euros after a playoff defeat to Wales.

news.title: Why play-off win may not send Wales to World Cup
news.lede: Victory over Albania extended Wales' unbeaten run to 10 matches, which is the longest sequence without defeat in their history. Wales will face Norway in the Women's World Cup play-off final knowing that even a famous victory may not be enough to send them to Brazil next summer. After Tuesday's semi-final success against Albania, Wales will play the home leg of the final at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December before the return in Norway four days later. A triumph against the Norwegians would be among Wales' greatest achievements – yet Rhian Wilkinson's players do not know if it would be enough to book a place at a first Women's World Cup.

news.title: Matildas’ 7-1 thumping papers over cracks in World Cup campaign
news.lede: The final auditions for Australia’s World Cup team are now underway, with eight months before Joe Montemurro picks his squad to board the plane for Brazil and important questions still to be answered despite a thumping finish to this international window. After a disappointing 4-2 defeat to Germany, the next generation of Matildas made the most of their chances and rallied together to beat Haiti 7-1. Australia’s World Cup stars led the younger generation to victory. Getty Images for Football Australia.

news.title: FIFA Technical Study Group Identifies Four Key Areas for African Teams to Improve After 2026 World Cup
news.lede: FIFA’s Technical Study Group has outlined four key areas African national teams must address to improve their competitiveness following their performances at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The recommendations focus on improving attacking efficiency, pressing higher up the pitch, managing matches more effectively in the closing stages and building on existing defensive strengths. One of the key areas highlighted is the need for African teams to create more goal scoring opportunities inside the penalty area rather than relying heavily on long range efforts. Improving movement, decision making and combinations in the final third could help teams become more clinical in front of goal.

news.title: FIFA Reaffirms Recognition of Ali Abdi Mohamed-Led Somalia Football Federation
news.lede: FIFA has confirmed that it has not opened an investigation into the situation within the Somalia Football Federation (SFF), reaffirming its recognition of the current Executive Committee led by President Ali Abdi Mohamed. The clarification represents a significant endorsement of the existing leadership as Somali football continues efforts to strengthen its structures, expand youth development and increase the country’s participation in international competitions. FIFA and the Confederation of African Football (CAF) continue to recognise the Ali Abdi Mohamed-led administration, maintaining their recognition of the federation’s current Executive Committee. Under President Ali’s leadership, Somalia has made progress in youth football development, with increased opportunities for young players to compete at regional and international levels.

news.title: FIFA set to propose 6.3 billion dollars funding for football development — report
news.lede: Reuters Reuters https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/cejkl7/article71564217.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/fifa%20logo.jpg Football’s world governing body planned to use the financial success of the latest World Cup to enhance investment in the sport’s development across 211 FIFA member associations, confederations and other stakeholders. SAO PAULO FIFA will propose to its members a $6.35 billion development fund for the next four-year cycle, including a boosted amount of $25 million for each national association, two people with knowledge of the plan and a letter reviewed by The Associated Press confirmed Tuesday. Football’s world governing body planned to use the financial success of the latest World Cup to enhance investment in the sport’s development across 211 FIFA member associations, confederations and other stakeholders.

news.title: Women’s football is growing fast — but players still face major gaps
news.lede: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for greater structure globally. At first glance, women's football is healthier than ever. A recent report by FIFPRO, football's global players' union, said worldwide revenue is expected to reach over $1bn (€894m) in 2027. The World Cup in Brazil, a first in South America, will be the last with 32 teams and is expected to be the most watched and biggest revenue-generating women's tournament ever.

news.title: FIFA World Cup 2030: Netflix gets all 104 matches in Spain; will fans still be able to watch for free?
news.lede: Imagine settling in to watch a World Cup match, only to discover that your usual television channel no longer carries it. Would you subscribe to a streaming service to catch every game, or stick to whatever is available for free? That is the question Spanish football fans are facing after Netflix secured the rights to all 104 matches of the 2030 FIFA World Cup in Spain and Andorra. Announced on October 13, the deal marks Netflix’s first broadcast of a major men’s international football tournament in Spain.
